cohort: 105,992 patients who delivered between 1991 and 2017 at a tertiary medical center
finding: Women who delivered by cesarean section had a significantly higher incidence of benign and malignant neoplasms, including uterine cancer, compared to those who delivered vaginally.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with a higher risk for malignancy-related hospitalizations but not specifically for uterine cancer after adjusting for confounders.
